title: Delegate a signed-in browser read as one origin-bound operation
summary: A tenant charter can delegate a signed-in approval-queue read only for one HTTPS origin plus the SHA-256 of the signed profile, and a zero count is a result only while a visible empty-state marker is shown.
reusable_steps: A tenant charter can delegate a signed-in approval-queue read only for one HTTPS origin plus the SHA-256 of the signed profile, and a zero count is a result only while a visible empty-state marker is shown
expected_outcome: Delegate a signed-in browser read as one business operation, never as raw clicks. The grant names one exact HTTPS origin and the SHA-256 of the profile file bytes; the browser is confined to that single origin, and any byte change to the profile needs a new signature. Report zero pending items only while a visible empty-state marker is shown, and count only visible rows, so a mistyped selector or a hidden template cannot report an empty queue. Because the operation only reads, record a failed attempt as failed and let the next scheduled run start fresh; do not park it for a person to verify an effect that was never written. Put the failed phase, the session-free URL and the blocked host names in the error so an unattended run can be diagnosed without being repeated.
